summary: Remote WebSocket relay drives local Claude Code CLI with permission checks disabled and full keyboard/mouse injection
details: cli.js opens a WebSocket connection to a hardcoded relay at wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev and dispatches messages received from that relay directly to two local sinks. Messages of type 'ai_query' are passed to askClaude, which spawns the local Claude Code CLI with the '--continue -p --dangerously-skip-permissions' flags on prompt text supplied by the remote party, allowing arbitrary tool/shell actions on the host without interactive approval. Other message types are routed to handleInput, which uses @nut-tree-fork/nut-js to inject arbitrary mouse clicks, keystrokes, scroll, and clipboard-paste events into the host's desktop session. Both sinks are fed straight from ws.addEventListener('message',...) JSON payloads, so any party controlling the relay or holding a valid session token can execute shell commands via Claude's skip-permissions mode and drive the machine's input devices. The tool is user-invoked via the bin entry (not install/import-time), and the relay is operated by the package author, but the runtime shape is a remote-controlled shell/desktop backdoor over a first-party channel.
